title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages): Grothendieck is working out a purely combinatorial 'analysis situs' in its one-dimensional case. L is a finite totally ordered set of vertices. M = M_0 ⊔ M_1 is the poset of cells, with points P_a (a ∈ L) and segments S_ab joining consecutive vertices. The specialization order is P_a ≤ S_ab and P_b ≤ S_ab. So M is a finite T0 (Alexandrov) model of a subdivided closed interval of R. 'Polygones'/'figures' are the constructible subsets of M. The 4 July section on the previous page sets out to classify them: each one splits into connected (convex) components, and this page lists the types of components.
(a) Closed convex (pre)figures are determined by an element T of Drap*(L). Here a 'flag' T is a non-empty set of consecutive vertices. The figure F_T consists of the P_a for a ∈ T together with the segments between consecutive elements of T. In particular F_T is the closure of its top cells, and T = F ∩ M_0 = F_0.
(b) Open convex figures: take T with card T ≥ 2. Define ∂F_T := ∂T = {min T, max T}, the two endpoints. Then Φ = F_T \ ∂F_T, using the identification of P_a with a (NB: 'on a fini par identifier les P_a aux a, i.e. M_0 à L').
(c) General case: take any subset α ⊂ ∂F and set Φ = F \ α.
Example: for card T = 2 this gives the closed, two half-open and open segments.
Conclusion: Préfigcom(M), the set of convex prefigures, is in bijection with the pairs (T, α), where T ∈ Drap*(L) and α ⊂ ∂T. By convention ∂F_T = ∅ when F_T = {P_a}. A marginal note sets F = closure of Φ (the smallest closed figure containing Φ) and ∂Φ := ∂F.
A crossed-out attempt defines an order on convex prefigures: Φ < Φ' iff x ≤_pos x' for all x ∈ Φ, x' ∈ Φ'. He notes this forces card(∂Φ ∩ ∂Φ') ≤ 1, and that a shared boundary point lies in neither Φ nor Φ'. This is the start of ordering the convex components of a polygon along the line.
Purpose: a normal form for constructible subsets of a finite combinatorial line, as finite ordered unions of intervals with specified open/closed ends. It is the 1-dimensional base case of the 'quatrième mouture' of the analysis situs project, which aims at a tame-topology foundation (Esquisse §5).
errors: Slip of notation: the manuscript writes 'α ∈ ∂T' in the identification with couples (T, α), but item c) uses α as a subset ('une partie α de ∂F'); it should read α ⊂ ∂T.
Φ = F \ ∂F mixes a subset of M with a subset of L; this is legitimate only through the stated identification M_0 ≅ L.

The convention ∂F_T = ∅ for card T = 1 is needed to make the bijection (T, α) consistent: otherwise T = {a} with α = {a} would give the empty set. He adds this in a correction, so the final text is consistent.
Otherwise correct: the classification of convex constructible subsets of a finite subdivided interval by endpoint data is elementary and right.

ideas.what: Combinatorial model of a 1-dimensional tame space as a finite poset of points and open segments (specialization order), with figures as constructible subsets
ideas.modern_name: Finite T0/Alexandrov space (face poset) of a subdivided interval; o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord (1966) for finite spaces; van den Dries et al. for o-minimal cell decomposition
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5; this combinatorial version is not published

ideas.what: Classification of convex (connected) constructible subsets as pairs (flag T of consecutive vertices, subset α of its two endpoints): closed, half-open and open intervals
ideas.modern_name: Intervals of a linearly ordered set / 1-cells with boundary data

ideas.what: Abortive ordering of convex components along the line (Φ < Φ' iff all points of Φ precede all points of Φ'), with remarks on shared boundary points
ideas.modern_name: Linear order on the connected components of a 1-dimensional definable set

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary bookkeeping: intervals in a finite combinatorial line classified by their endpoint data. It has historical interest only as part of the unpublished 1986 'Analysis situs' drafts; there is no new mathematics here.
transcription_corrections: First item marker '•)' is almost certainly 'a)' (items a), b), c) follow).
'Drap^α(L)' should read 'Drap*(L)' (non-empty flags), consistent with the next page.
'α ∈ ∂T' in the line '(T, α), T ∈ Drap*(L), α ∈ ∂T' is as written but means α ⊂ ∂T.
In b) the reading is 'elles sont données par T ∈ Drap*(L), card T ≥ 2, et une partie de'; the struck word before 'elles' is likely 'cas de'.
Marginal note reads approximately: 'On pose F = Φ̄ (plus petite figure fermée contenant Φ) et ∂F = ∂Φ' — the second identity reversed (∂Φ := ∂F).
